text:
alex: hey, quick heads-up — running `terraform apply` in staging hung with a state lock then the subsequent plan shows a resource marked tainted that we didn't touch. anyone seen aws_iam_policy_attachment get flagged after we imported the policy last week? :eyes:

maria: can you paste the plan output? also which backend (s3 + dynamo)?

alex: backend is s3+dynamo in us-west-2. plan snippet:```
An execution plan has been generated and is shown below.
Resource actions are indicated with the following symbols:~ destroy and then create replacement

# aws_iam_policy_attachment.prod_attach will be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_iam_policy_attachment" "prod_attach" {
    ~ id       = "policy-attach-123" -> (known after apply)
      # (other attributes omitted)
  }
```

sam: did we import with the exact same resource address? if someone did `terraform import aws_iam_policy_attachment.prod_attach something` but the state path differs it can create a dup/taint

alex: I used `terraform import aws_iam_policy_attachment.prod_attach policy-attach-123` last Tuesday. no other imports since.

jen: quick checks: run `terraform state show aws_iam_policy_attachment.prod_attach` and `terraform plan -refresh=true` — see if refresh flips it back. also check dynamodb for stale lock.

alex: ran `terraform state show` output looks normal, attachment refs present. `terraform plan -refresh=true` still wants replace.

maria: could be that the imported resource has computed attributes (like roles list order) that differ vs config. try `terraform state pull` and inspect the stored attributes for ordering.

sam: alternate: if it's safe, you can `terraform state rm aws_iam_policy_attachment.prod_attach` then `terraform import` again — sometimes re-importing with exact address fixes computed diffs. but be careful if other resources depend on it.

alex: also noticed apply earlier failed with `Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException` and then a CI runner got stuck. ops-bot showed a lock held by run/2378. I cleared that with the REST endpoint after confirming it's stale.

jen: good you cleared. if the lock was held during a partial apply, state may be inconsistent. check `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` to get more certainty.

alex: tried `state rm` + re-import on a clone workspace — re-import solved the taint on the clone, plan is clean there. planning to do the same in staging but want to confirm procedure.

maria: safest flow for staging: 1) take a snapshot `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-tf-state/staging.tfstate ./staging.tfstate.bak` 2) `terraform state rm aws_iam_policy_attachment.prod_attach` 3) `terraform import aws_iam_policy_attachment.prod_attach policy-attach-123` 4) `terraform plan -refresh=true` 5) if clean, run `terraform apply` during a maintenance window.

sam: also double-check IAM propagation/consistency; if the attachment references a role that was recreated, the ARN may differ. `aws iam get-role --role-name X` to confirm.

alex: noted. one more Q: any objections to doing the import during low traffic at 0100 PST?

jen: no objections. @ops-bot please annotate the change in the incident log and add a short outage window 0100-0200 PST. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: noted — added annotation: "staging terraform state re-import for aws_iam_policy_attachment (0100-0200 PST)"

alex: thanks team — i'll follow the steps and report back. if I hit anything weird I'll ping in this thread. :pray:
